# ARLOVI — COMPLETE PRODUCT UX & NATIVE APPLICATION SPECIFICATION
**Edition:** 1.0  |  **Issued:** 14 November 2026  |  **Status:** Engineering design handoff; implementations unverified
**Directive:** Complete target product. No MVP, no reduced launch scope and no knowingly inert feature placeholders.
**Working name:** Arlovi, subject to trademark/domain clearance. Routes and brand assets must be rename-ready.

## Document coverage
- 35 native workspace/application domains; 316 individually registered screen contracts; 1323 tab instances; 956 contextual overlay instances; 1328 named primary actions; 20 end-to-end workflows.
- Tab, overlay and action contracts are scoped to their owning screen and inherit the shared component accessibility/state standards.
- Feature completeness is the desired final product contract, not evidence that these features currently exist.

## A. Product and governance mandate
### Product mandate
Arlovi is the complete AI-native digital headquarters and native business application suite. The approved target is not an MVP and has no features designated as disposable placeholders. Parallel engineering workstreams and sequencing of dependencies are execution mechanics only; the product contract covers all listed capabilities.

### Design-source status
This handoff is a product UX and application-behaviour specification produced from the established concept. It is not evidence that pages, integrations, accounting compliance, creative engines or agent features have already been implemented. All implementation states remain unverified until engineering and QA supply evidence.

### Platform identity
Arlovi is a working name subject to legal and domain clearance. All IDs and routes intentionally treat the branding as replaceable through a single configuration; screen contracts and domain models must not depend on the brand spelling.

### Primary actors
Organization owner, CEO, executive assistant, department manager, specialist employee, external partner/customer, IT operator, security/privacy administrator, AI Chief of Staff, department AI leaders, worker agents and independent QA agents. An AI employee is explicitly machine-identified and not a human employee or source of authority.

### Navigation model
Persistent organization switcher and command search; personal Home; conversation; Missions; Team; Apps; Inbox; Insights; department spaces. Deep links carry organization scope; subordinate applications can have their own second-level navigation. Opening tools must not discard unsaved context.

### Decision and execution model
Agents propose work from source-attributed context; centralized independent policy checks mission grant, role, resource, budget and time conditions; durable worker executes approved capability; authoritative external or native verification writes an action receipt; UI reports actual state.

### Native and connected parity
All native apps share canonical identity, events, files, authorization, search, audit, knowledge, analytics and AI capabilities. External connectors remain optional and are never silently replaced or used without approval. Banking, payment rails, outbound communication delivery and regulatory functions may rely on licensed providers underneath native UX.

### Document coverage rule
Every screen registry entry has its own ID, route, purpose, primary content regions, tabs, actions, overlay inventory, agent behaviour, exceptional condition and verification checklist. The shared pattern specifications below are inherited by every matching component; app overrides control business-specific behaviour.

## B. Layout and interface design tokens
- **Header — 60px:** Persistent org/context, command search, status, notification and profile actions; 56px permitted for constrained width
- **Expanded navigation — 248px:** Collapses to icon rail of 64px or mobile sheet
- **Secondary app navigation — 208–240px:** Application routes and user preferences; overlays in constrained windows
- **Context inspector — 300–360px:** Resizes where appropriate; overlay or bottom sheet below 1200px
- **Editor toolbar — 48–56px:** Sticky within editor; contextual overflow at narrow width
- **Status bar — 28–32px:** Only when needed for editor coordinates, save state or runtime details
- **Comfortable body text — 16px / 1.5 line height:** Normal reading, messages, business explanations
- **Dense data — 13–14px / 1.4:** Professional tables with user-controlled density; never shrink fundamental text on mobile
- **Section headings — 20–24px:** Contrast and hierarchy without excessive vertical waste
- **Page heading — 28–32px:** Fluid clamp with room for actions and localization
- **Input/control — 40–48px:** 44px preferred main pointer/touch target; larger where needed
- **Page gutter — 32px desktop / 24px tablet / 16px mobile:** Constrained reading max width 720–840px; canvases and tables fill available space
- **Standard card padding — 16–24px:** Compact density may reduce to 12px; preserve hit targets
- **Dialog widths — 440–640px typical:** Task-dependent; avoid stacking modals
- **Motion — 120–260ms typical:** Fast 120ms; panel 200–260ms; preference for reduced-motion
- **Viewport — 100dvh with fallback:** Independent scroll regions and mobile keyboard/safe-area handling

### Responsive contracts
- **compact (320–599 CSS px):** single primary column; bottom navigation; inspector/fullscreen sheets
- **medium (600–899 CSS px):** 1–2 content columns; compact navigation; touch-first controls
- **expanded (900–1199 CSS px):** 64px rail; panels overlay or toggle; constrained toolbars
- **desktop (1200–1599 CSS px):** 248px sidebar + work region; optional 320px inspector
- **wide (1600+ CSS px):** multi-pane specialist tools; maximal reading widths remain bounded

### Standard UI states
empty, initializing, loading, loaded, editing, saving, pending external confirmation, verified, partial, blocked, error, offline, read-only, conflict, archived.

## C. Shared interface contracts
### Global header
**Function:** Org/workspace switch, breadcrumb, universal search, active-work indicator, notifications and profile. Show selected org distinctly; changes cannot leave old-org resources in context.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Keyboard navigation, focus after switching, command search, accessible status.

### Application sidebar
**Function:** Active route, app grouping, pinned sections, badges, collapsed rail, scroll, resizing and role visibility. Local app nav appears only when useful.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Persist per-user collapse state; route changes preserve page filters where appropriate.

### Tabs
**Function:** Each tab has unique content model and URI/query state as appropriate; roving keyboard focus; scrollable overflow and visible selected indicator.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Preserve unsaved edits and warn before destructive tab transition.

### Context inspector
**Function:** Record/element/agent detail at 300–360px desktop; user-controlled resize, close, focus return.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Mobile sheet with heading, reachable close, nontrapping when nonmodal.

### Drawer
**Function:** Contextual details, forms and record inspector; appropriate overlay/backdrop and URL state.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Escape closes when safe, unsaved changes prompt, focus restored, swipe behavior not exclusive.

### Modal
**Function:** Only for focused consequential decisions or scoped multistep form. Meaningful title, primary/secondary actions, explicit side effects.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Focus trap, return focus, disabled conditions explained, no nested modal chains.

### Popover
**Function:** Anchored controls, shortcuts or small selection. Auto-flip against viewport, high-contrast focus.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Dismiss on Escape/outside click unless state requires deliberate submission.

### Toolbar
**Function:** Grouped commands by relevance, selected tool state, shortcut hints, overflow strategy.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Touch and keyboard equivalents; unsupported action visibly disabled with reason.

### Table
**Function:** Saved column settings, sort/filter/search, virtualization, row select and bulk actions, stable IDs.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Numbers aligned and tabular; mobile accessible cards/alternate where feasible.

### Board
**Function:** Visible card identity, owner, state, order and drop zones; moving can trigger explicit rules only.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Move via menu/keyboard as alternative to drag; reject invalid transition clearly.

### Calendar
**Function:** Resource/timezone display, available holds vs confirmed bookings, conflicts, accessible agenda.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** DST boundary handling, recurrence edits, drag alternative and period navigation.

### Canvas
**Function:** Select/pan/zoom/undo/redo; layers hierarchy; coordinates; device preview; snapping; source/edit fidelity.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** No forced rasterization; alternate object list and keyboard object transforms.

### Timeline
**Function:** Time-scale, ordering, dependencies, clip/task/event selection, zoom and snapping.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Access via chronological list; handle timezone/frame precision and move confirmation.

### Rich editor
**Function:** Autosave with explicit save state; comments, versions, formatting, AI diff, accurate export.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Conflicting edits resolved and version history immutable.

### AI composer
**Function:** Natural text, voice, attachments, mentions, context scope, task type and action confirmation.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** External sources untrusted; inference never bypasses permission or user review.

### Notification
**Function:** Typed priority, source, grouped updates, read/acknowledged/resolved, target deep-link, preference and expiry.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Read never equals approved; avoid toast storm and hidden critical incidents.

### Approval sheet
**Function:** Identifies requesting agent/human, exact action, scope, affected records, reversibility, cost, constraints, expiry.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Server-side plan-hash and version check before execution.

### Action receipt
**Function:** Status of requested/accepted/pending/verified/failed action, provider resource ID, evidence, actor and grant.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Timed-out irreversible action reconciled before any retry.

### Error banner
**Function:** Clear cause, scope of impact, confirmed actions, proposed recovery and owner.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** No fake success; persistent recovery entry for long-lived incidents.

### File upload
**Function:** Drag/drop and picker, progress, type/size limits, security scan, parsing, source classification and proposed use.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Untrusted content never becomes agent authority; cancellation/failed chunk recovery.

### Search & command
**Function:** Unified result groups, saved recents, keyboard activation, command preview and cross-org boundary.
**Keyboard/responsive/verification:** Resource-level permissions checked on every result and action.

### ARL-HQ-001 — Executive Home
**Route:** `/o/:org/hq/home` · **Layout:** dashboard · **Audience:** CEO; Founder; operations lead; department manager; member; AI Chief of Staff
**User job / page intent:** The company-wide digital office: executive intelligence, personal work, departments, locations, company goals, and shared operational context. This screen specializes in executive home; it must deliver its primary job without requiring navigation to an unrelated app.
**Content hierarchy and regions:** Personal greeting and AI composer; performance summary with source freshness; urgent approvals; active missions; recommended insights.
**Layout contract:** KPI/briefing modular grid. Start with one-line summary, then top decisions, metrics, work and source links. **Responsive:** 3-4 columns wide; 2 columns tablet; 1 column narrow, card reorder via menu.
**Page-specific tabs / navigation:**
- **Today:** The today subsection of Executive Home; show only related today records, with owner, current state, relevant dates, source and permission-aware actions.
- **Week:** The week subsection of Executive Home; show only related week records, with owner, current state, relevant dates, source and permission-aware actions.
- **Saved views:** The saved views subsection of Executive Home; show only related saved views records, with owner, current state, relevant dates, source and permission-aware actions.
**Primary interactions:**
- Ask Chief of Staff: make the intended state change explicit, validate eligibility and permissions, confirm saved/verified result and expose undo or recovery where applicable.
- rearrange cards: make the intended state change explicit, validate eligibility and permissions, confirm saved/verified result and expose undo or recovery where applicable.
- drill into metric: update the focused view without losing filters or record identity; reveal source and detail through navigable inspector or route.
- dismiss recommendation: make the intended state change explicit, validate eligibility and permissions, confirm saved/verified result and expose undo or recovery where applicable.
**Overlays and secondary interface contracts:**
- Widget picker — scoped editor with labeled fields, required/optional validation, keyboard support, draft persistence, submit/cancel and inline errors.
- metric inspector — contextual drawer/side panel exposing the selected record, evidence and linked actions; preserve parent view, URL selection and focus return.
- save view dialog — contextual overlay with explicit trigger, titled content, resource context, focus management, escape/close, responsive placement and safe action feedback.
**AI responsibility:** Synthesizes attributable executive briefing from permitted data; opens investigation missions only by policy. The AI is identified as automated, uses authorized source context, and dispatches consequential operations through the policy gateway.
**Data and access:** Data entities: Organization; Workspace; Department; Membership; Objective; Location; Briefing. All visible records, search results, related documents and actions are organization-scoped, role-authorized, version-aware and source-attributed.
**States and edge case:** Support relevant global states; particular requirement: Unknown or stale KPI must show age and unavailable source, not a fabricated value.
**Page acceptance checks:**
- [ ] Route /o/:org/hq/home loads only scoped organization data for an authorized role; direct URL access to an unauthorized organization is denied.
- [ ] Switching between Today and Saved views shows the correct distinct content, preserves relevant state, supports keyboard activation and an accessible selected-state announcement.
- [ ] The action “Ask Chief of Staff” performs its stated change or navigation with loading, validation, explicit success/failed state and a traceable record when consequential.
- [ ] The “Widget picker” overlay is accessible, context-specific, resizes on mobile and returns focus without losing unsaved work.
- [ ] Edge test: Unknown or stale KPI must show age and unavailable source, not a fabricated value; verify denial/fallback, status language, audit/event and safe recovery.

## E. End-to-end cross-application workflows
### WF-01 — Company onboarding
**Flow:** Owner creates organization -> validates website or files -> optionally connects providers -> approves Company Brain profile -> assigns AI team -> configures authority -> creates first mission.
**Validation:** Organization identity, source provenance, plan approvals, no unauthorized connector access.

### WF-02 — Cross-department campaign
**Flow:** Chief of Staff researches commerce/finance -> Marketing and Creative produce plan/assets -> Finance checks margin -> owner approves -> tools publish -> receipts verify -> Insights reports.
**Validation:** Spend reservation, publishing scopes, consent, asset rights, provider confirmation, rollback limitations.

### WF-03 — Revenue decline investigation
**Flow:** Owner asks -> Finance reconciles actuals -> Commerce/Marketing/Sales compare drivers -> report separates fact/hypothesis -> plan with assumptions -> explicit change approvals.
**Validation:** Source freshness, double-count prevention, attribution uncertainty.

### WF-04 — Customer request to resolution
**Flow:** Request enters Service -> contact verified -> AI answers from approved KB or escalates -> order/booking/finance updates if authorized -> customer notified -> case closed with evidence.
**Validation:** Identity, privacy, service SLA and no double-refund.

### WF-05 — Sales-to-cash
**Flow:** Lead -> CRM qualify -> proposal -> quote approval -> customer acceptance -> project/order -> invoice -> bank reconciliation -> reporting.
**Validation:** Canonical customer ID, accepted price version, financial posting and audit.

### WF-06 — Hire-to-onboard
**Flow:** HR opens position -> candidate reviews -> approved offer -> employee record -> IT access request -> training/calendar -> payroll inputs -> manager signoff.
**Validation:** Applicant retention, discrimination safeguards, identity and payroll approvals.

### WF-07 — Design-to-publish
**Flow:** Creative brief -> Brand Intelligence -> editable Studio file -> human+AI reviews -> responsive/accessibility QA -> approved publish -> versioned live output.
**Validation:** Editable structure, brand rules, asset licensing, provider confirmation.

### WF-08 — Build-to-deploy
**Flow:** App brief -> data/roles architecture -> visual+code builder -> sandbox tests -> security/UX QA -> stage -> production approval -> monitor -> rollback if warranted.
**Validation:** Environment isolation, no secret exposure, release gates.

### WF-09 — Document-to-knowledge
**Flow:** Upload -> antivirus/validation -> extract -> classify -> canonical mapping -> discrepancy review -> approve fact -> scoped retrieval -> retention and correction.
**Validation:** Prompt injection, GDPR/retention, source-to-fact traceability.

### WF-10 — Booking-to-service
**Flow:** Customer selects service -> real inventory/staff available -> reserve slot -> payment/deposit -> confirm -> reminders -> check-in -> completion -> invoice/service history.
**Validation:** Atomic slot holds, timezone, cancellation policy and receipts.

### WF-11 — Replenishment-to-payment
**Flow:** Stock threshold -> forecast -> requisition -> policy approval -> PO -> supplier acknowledgment -> receipt/scan -> AP bill -> payment authorization -> reconciliation.
**Validation:** Supplier identity, physical evidence, ledger consistency, spend cap.

### WF-12 — Connector incident recovery
**Flow:** Health warning -> dedupe incident -> classify provider/internal -> safe retry or repair -> owner reconnect if required -> authoritative verification -> resume queued missions.
**Validation:** Unknown side effects, no privilege escalation, auditable resolution.

### WF-13 — AI workforce lifecycle
**Flow:** Create agent contract -> assign model/skill -> scoped data and actions -> evaluate scenarios -> owner activates -> mission assignments -> review metrics -> suspend/retire.
**Validation:** Agent not self-authorizing, avoid unsafe model degradation.

### WF-14 — Notification and approval
**Flow:** Event -> attention policy -> eligible recipients -> bundled notice -> inspect exact scope -> step-up where needed -> approve/deny -> mission update -> receipt.
**Validation:** Read != resolved, organization isolation, delivery receipts.

### WF-15 — Monthly executive reporting
**Flow:** Data freshness checks -> ledger/CRM/operations aggregation -> finance reconciliation -> AI insight drafting -> reviewer approval -> on-brand Docs/Present output -> authorized distribution.
**Validation:** No fabricated statistics, recipients, version and audit controls.

### WF-16 — External client collaboration
**Flow:** Project share grant -> portal invitation -> client authenticates -> accesses only scoped records -> comments/approves/pays -> native tasks and audit sync.
**Validation:** No cross-client leakage or arbitrary sharing inheritance.

### WF-17 — Multi-entity organization
**Flow:** Owner changes legal entity or brand -> UI scopes route, currency, locale and records -> AI context reset -> transactions remain within entity.
**Validation:** Cross-tenant and cross-entity access cannot be assumed.

### WF-18 — Personal-device continuation
**Flow:** Begin on desktop -> autosaved document/mission -> mobile authenticated session -> responsive state restores -> action approver confirms -> desktop reflects update.
**Validation:** Concurrent change detection, private device notifications.

### WF-19 — Sensitive data deletion/export
**Flow:** Authorized request -> retention/legal hold review -> scoped export or deletion jobs -> downstream connector requests -> verification -> evidence certificate.
**Validation:** Deletion cannot break legally required immutable audits.

### WF-20 — Company emergency pause
**Flow:** Authorized owner triggers pause -> execution dispatch prevented -> queued jobs checkpoint -> external side effects listed -> targeted revoke/escalation -> safe resume.
**Validation:** Cannot falsely claim that accepted third-party actions were reversed.

## F. Security, QA and failure containment
- Cross-organization or cross-brand leakage in retrieval, caches, search, file previews and notifications.
- Indirect prompt injection through customer uploads, email, external webpages, model outputs or connector tool responses.
- Non-idempotent irreversible actions retried after network timeout.
- Unbounded AI delegation, token use, concurrency or external media-render spend.
- Approval based on stale plan version or modified external account.
- Autonomous accounting/payroll/legal/employment actions outside human signoff.
- Conflicting or stale canonical data leading to a wrong business recommendation.
- Inaccessible canvas/drag UI without keyboard/single-pointer equivalent.
- Duplicate customer identities after external sync with different providers.
- Incorrect time zones, DST transitions or locale-sensitive money/date operations.
- Unverified business outcomes wrongly labelled complete.
- Insufficient native feature parity creating false claims of replacing specialist tools.
- Provider rate limits, licensing, outages and schema evolution.
- Lost work from autosave race, conflicting edits or mobile navigation.
- No suitable graceful degradation for partial connectivity or device limitations.

## G. Definition of production-grade completeness
- [ ] Each registry entry maps to approved designs, implemented route, integrated backend, data contract, permission policy, tests and owner.
- [ ] Every named action and overlay is functional or is visibly and truthfully blocked with a reason and next step. No fake success states.
- [ ] Specialist apps pass task-based acceptance with domain practitioners, not just visual screenshot review.
- [ ] All AI capabilities are exercised with normal, malicious, missing-data, stale-data, denied-access, interrupted-network and external-failure cases.
- [ ] Native accounting, payroll, payment, communications, security, regulated and legal functions must complete applicable specialist certification/review where required.
- [ ] Every page, tab and overlay has desktop/tablet/mobile, keyboard, screen reader, colour contrast, 200/400% zoom and reduced-motion verification.
- [ ] Unverified functionality stays labelled as unverified. The document describes intended requirements, not existing product capability.

- **WCAG 2.2 Recommendation:** https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ — W3C accessibility target; contrast, reflow, target size, dragging alternatives and status messages.
- **WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices:** https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/ — Interaction semantics for tablists, dialogs, menus, grids and trees.
- **WAI-ARIA 1.2:** https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/ — Roles, states, properties and keyboard focus expectations.
- **Figma Auto Layout guide:** https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040451373-Guide-to-auto-layout-in-Figma — Responsive frame sizing, padding and adaptable content.
- **Adaptive Material layout guidance:** https://developer.android.com/codelabs/adaptive-material-guidance — Responsive window size classes and layout adaptation.
